question_html: Which of the following expenditures generates enduring benefits and helps in revenue generation over more than one accounting period?

options.B: Capital expenditure

answer_html: Answer: (B) Capital expenditure generates enduring benefits and helps in revenue generation over more than one accounting period[cite: 49].

question_html: Why is the distinction between capital and revenue expenditure critical in accounting?

options.A: To determine whether an item should be placed in the Profit and Loss Account or the Balance Sheet.
options.B: To calculate the exact physical weight of factory machinery.
options.C: To avoid paying municipal property taxes entirely.
options.D: To ensure all cash inflows equal cash outflows daily.

answer_html: Answer: (A) To determine whether an item should be placed in the Profit and Loss Account or the Balance Sheet.

question_html: For a trader dealing in office furniture, the purchase of furniture for resale is classified as:

options.B: Revenue expenditure

answer_html: Answer: (B) Revenue expenditure
topic_text: Considerations in Determining Capital and Revenue Expenditures

question_html: Overhaul expenses incurred to put a second-hand machinery in working condition are treated as:

options.A: Revenue expenditure because the machine is old
options.B: Capital expenditure because they provide an endurable long-term advantage
options.D: Directly expensed to the Profit and Loss Account in the current period

answer_html: Answer: (B) Capital expenditure because they provide an endurable long-term advantage.

question_html: Legal fees paid to acquire ownership rights over a property are classified as:

options.B: Capital expenditure

answer_html: Answer: (B) Capital expenditure

question_html: Legal expenses incurred to defend a suit claiming that the firm's factory site belongs to a plaintiff are treated as:

options.A: Capital expenditure because it relates to a fixed asset site
options.B: Revenue expenditure because it is a maintenance expense that neither adds new capacity nor creates new enduring benefits
options.D: Deferred revenue charges amortised over 10 years

answer_html: Answer: (B) Revenue expenditure because it is a maintenance expense that neither adds new capacity nor creates new enduring benefits.

question_html: Amount spent for the replacement of a worn-out part of a machine is classified as:

options.B: Revenue expenditure

answer_html: Answer: (B) Revenue expenditure

question_html: Initial repairs and whitewashing expenses incurred upon purchasing an old, second-hand building to put it into usable condition are:

options.A: Revenue expenses because the building is old
options.B: Capital expenditure because they form part of the cost of acquiring a usable asset

answer_html: Answer: (B) Capital expenditure because they form part of the cost of acquiring a usable asset.

question_html: Expenses incurred in connection with obtaining a statutory license to run a cinema hall are treated as:

options.B: Capital expenditure (pre-operative expense to be amortised)

answer_html: Answer: (B) Capital expenditure (pre-operative expense to be amortised)

question_html: The cost of constructing temporary huts that were necessary for the construction of a cinema house and demolished when the building was ready is:

options.B: Capital expenditure, added to the total construction cost of the cinema house
options.C: Written off immediately as miscellaneous loss
options.D: Treated as a separate intangible asset

answer_html: Answer: (B) Capital expenditure, added to the total construction cost of the cinema house.

question_html: Amount paid for the removal of inventory to a new site is classified as:

options.B: Revenue expenditure

answer_html: Answer: (B) Revenue expenditure

question_html: Changing the rings and pistons of an engine at a cost to achieve better fuel efficiency is treated as:

options.A: Revenue expenditure because engine parts are routinely replaced
options.B: Capital expenditure because it improves fixed asset performance and reduces future running costs

answer_html: Answer: (B) Capital expenditure because it improves fixed asset performance and reduces future running costs.

question_html: Security deposit money paid to a telephone company for installing a telephone in the office is classified as:

options.B: Capital expenditure
options.C: An asset (deposit) adjusted against future bills

answer_html: Answer: (C) An asset (deposit) adjusted against future bills.

question_html: Receipts obtained in the ordinary course of normal business activities (e.g., sale of goods, interest income) are:

options.B: Revenue receipts

answer_html: Answer: (B) Revenue receipts

question_html: How are capital receipts treated in financial accounting?

options.A: Directly credited in full to the Profit and Loss Account
options.B: Shown in the Balance Sheet or used to reduce asset book value / create liabilities or equity, with only profit/loss credited to P&L
options.C: Ignored entirely from all financial records

answer_html: Answer: (B) Shown in the Balance Sheet or used to reduce asset book value / create liabilities or equity, with only profit/loss credited to P&L.

question_html: A machine with a book value of ₹10,00,000 is sold for ₹12,00,000. What is the nature of the ₹12,00,000 receipt and how is the gain treated?

options.A: Revenue receipt; full ₹12,00,000 credited to P&L
options.B: Capital receipt of ₹12,00,000 with the profit of ₹2,00,000 credited to Profit and Loss Account
options.D: Capital receipt with zero impact on P&L

answer_html: Answer: (B) Capital receipt of ₹12,00,000 with the profit of ₹2,00,000 credited to Profit and Loss Account.

question_html: Premium received on the issue of shares is classified as:

options.B: Capital receipt

answer_html: Answer: (B) Capital receipt

question_html: On the maturity of a bank fixed deposit, the principal amount received back is a ________ and the interest received is a ________.

options.B: Capital receipt; Revenue receipt

answer_html: Answer: (B) Capital receipt; Revenue receipt.

question_html: A company pays a fine of ₹1,000 for contravening business rules and also pays ₹2,000 as a license renewal fee for the next year. How are these classified?

options.B: Fine is revenue expenditure; renewal fee for next year is a prepaid expense (asset)
options.D: Fine is capital expenditure; renewal fee is revenue expense for current year

answer_html: Answer: (B) Fine is revenue expenditure; renewal fee for next year is a prepaid expense (asset).

question_html: Overhauling expenses of ₹25,000 incurred for the engine of a motor car to achieve better fuel efficiency are:

options.B: Capital expenditure because they yield a long-term advantage by reducing future running costs

answer_html: Answer: (B) Capital expenditure because they yield a long-term advantage by reducing future running costs.

question_html: Inauguration expenses of ₹25 lakhs incurred on the opening of a new manufacturing unit in an existing business are classified as:

options.A: Capital expenditure because it relates to a new unit
options.B: Revenue expenditure because such expenses do not generate an enduring benefit over more than one accounting period
options.D: Fully capitalized as part of factory land

answer_html: Answer: (B) Revenue expenditure because such expenses do not generate an enduring benefit over more than one accounting period.

question_html: Compensation paid to workers who opted for voluntary retirement (VRS) is generally in the nature of:

options.B: Revenue expenditure (often deferred over future years due to its large magnitude)
options.D: Direct addition to fixed asset book value

answer_html: Answer: (B) Revenue expenditure (often deferred over future years due to its large magnitude).

question_html: Travelling expenses of directors incurred on trips abroad specifically for the purchase of capital assets are:

options.B: Capital expenditure

answer_html: Answer: (B) Capital expenditure

question_html: Amount spent on the demolition of an old building to construct a bigger building on the same site is treated as:

options.B: Capital expenditure (part of the cost of the new building)

answer_html: Answer: (B) Capital expenditure (part of the cost of the new building).

question_html: Insurance claim received on account of a machinery damaged by fire is classified as:

options.B: Capital receipt

answer_html: Answer: (B) Capital receipt

question_html: Renovating restaurant cabins in a manner that creates extra space and increases the number of cabins from 10 to 13 at a cost of ₹20,000 is:

options.A: Revenue expenditure because it is called renovation
options.B: Capital expenditure because it enhances the future revenue-generating capability and capacity of the business

answer_html: Answer: (B) Capital expenditure because it enhances the future revenue-generating capability and capacity of the business.

question_html: Legal expenses incurred by a financing company to recover overdue installment payments from defaulting customers are:

options.B: Revenue expenditure (normal recurring business expense)

answer_html: Answer: (B) Revenue expenditure (normal recurring business expense).

question_html: Transportation costs incurred for bringing a newly purchased machinery to the factory site are classified as:

options.B: Capital expenditure

answer_html: Answer: (B) Capital expenditure

question_html: Entrance fees received by a social club (like Ram and Shyam Social Club) are treated as:

options.B: Revenue receipt

answer_html: Answer: (A) Capital receipt

question_html: A subsidy received from the government for working capital by a manufacturing concern is classified as:

options.B: Revenue receipt

answer_html: Answer: (B) Revenue receipt

question_html: Interest received on investments is classified as:

options.B: Revenue receipt

answer_html: Answer: (B) Revenue receipt

question_html: Amount received as a medium-term loan from a financial institution (like IDBI) for augmenting working capital is:

options.B: Revenue expenditure

answer_html: Answer: (C) Capital receipt

question_html: If repair cost is ₹25,000, whitewash expenses are ₹5,000 (both for an existing building), cost of building extension is ₹2,50,000, and cost of electrical wiring system improvement is ₹19,000, what is the total amount to be charged as expenses (P&L)?
answer_html: Answer: (C) ₹30,000 (Repair ₹25,000 + Whitewash ₹5,000; extension and wiring improvements are capitalised).

question_html: Which of the following is NOT a basic consideration in distinguishing between capital and revenue expenditures?

options.B: Recurring nature of expenditure
options.C: Personal income tax bracket of the business owner
options.D: Effect on revenue-generating capacity of the business

answer_html: Answer: (C) Personal income tax bracket of the business owner.
topic_text: Considerations in Determining Capital and Revenue Expenditures

question_html: Prepaid expenses represent future expenses paid in advance and are shown in the balance sheet as:

options.B: An asset

answer_html: Answer: (B) An asset.

question_html: Revenue from the sale of products is ordinarily reported as part of earnings in the period in which:

options.B: The cash is collected.

answer_html: Answer: (A) The sale is made.

question_html: Best Tech Solutions buys and sells computers as its main business. It purchases 20 computers for resale at ₹20,000 each and 1 computer for its accountant at ₹24,000. How are these classified?

options.B: 20 computers for resale (₹4,00,000) are revenue expenditure (purchase of stock); 1 computer for the accountant (₹24,000) is capital expenditure
options.D: 20 computers are capital assets; 1 computer is an operating expense

answer_html: Answer: (B) 20 computers for resale (₹4,00,000) are revenue expenditure (purchase of stock); 1 computer for the accountant (₹24,000) is capital expenditure.

question_html: Good Pictures Ltd. purchases second-hand furniture for ₹9,000, incurs ₹1,000 on repainting, and pays ₹200 to its own workmen for installation. What is the total capitalised cost of the furniture?
answer_html: Answer: (C) ₹10,200 (Purchase ₹9,000 + Repainting ₹1,000 + Installation wages ₹200).

question_html: An entity pays fire insurance of ₹1,000 on 1st October, 2021 for one year. For the accounting year ending 31st March, 2022, how much is treated as a revenue expense and how much as prepaid?

options.B: ₹500 as revenue expense for the current year and ₹500 as prepaid expense (asset)

answer_html: Answer: (B) ₹500 as revenue expense for the current year and ₹500 as prepaid expense (asset).

question_html: Which of the following is incurred to maintain the earning capacity of a business rather than enhance its productive capacity?

options.B: Revenue expenditure

answer_html: Answer: (B) Revenue expenditure.

question_html: What is the primary determinant for transferring an expenditure to the Profit and Loss Account?

options.A: The time factor (utilization of benefit in the particular accounting year)
options.B: The physical color of the asset purchased
options.C: The gender of the accountant recording the entry
options.D: The total number of employees in the firm

answer_html: Answer: (A) The time factor (utilization of benefit in the particular accounting year).

question_html: Money spent with the intention of reducing future operating/working expenses is generally classified as:

options.A: Revenue expenditure because it relates to operations
options.B: Capital expenditure because such cost reductions generate long-term enduring benefits to the entity

answer_html: Answer: (B) Capital expenditure because such cost reductions generate long-term enduring benefits to the entity.

question_html: How are revenue receipts recognized and treated in accounting?

options.A: Recognized on accrual basis as soon as the right of receipt is established and credited directly to the Profit and Loss Account
options.B: Credited directly to Capital account without P&L recognition
options.C: Treated as balance sheet liabilities indefinitely
options.D: Ignored until cash is physically received

answer_html: Answer: (A) Recognized on accrual basis as soon as the right of receipt is established and credited directly to the Profit and Loss Account.

question_html: Which of the following is an example of a revenue expenditure?

options.B: Monthly salary paid to accounting staff
options.C: Cost of building an extension to the warehouse
options.D: Legal fees to acquire land title

answer_html: Answer: (B) Monthly salary paid to accounting staff.

question_html: Why is the distinction between capital and revenue expenditure often considered difficult in practice?

options.A: Because tax laws forbid keeping accounting records
options.B: Because in many cases the borderline between maintenance and enhancement of an asset is very thin
options.C: Because accounting software automatically classifies all transactions as revenue
options.D: Because capital expenditures never appear in financial statements

answer_html: Answer: (B) Because in many cases the borderline between maintenance and enhancement of an asset is very thin.

question_html: How does the matching concept link with capital and revenue expenditures?

options.A: Revenue expenditures are charged in the current period, whereas capital expenditures are capitalized and charged to P&L based on the utilization of their benefits over future periods.
options.B: All expenditures must be charged immediately on day one regardless of benefit period.
options.C: Capital expenditures are never expensed through P&L.
options.D: Matching concept only applies to cash sales.

answer_html: Answer: (A) Revenue expenditures are charged in the current period, whereas capital expenditures are capitalized and charged to P&L based on the utilization of their benefits over future periods[cite: 49].

question_html: Which of the following represents a capital receipt?

options.B: Commission earned on services
options.C: Proceeds from the sale of fixed assets

answer_html: Answer: (C) Proceeds from the sale of fixed assets.

question_html: What is the effect on the financial statements if a capital expenditure is erroneously treated as a revenue expenditure?

options.A: Net profit for the current year is understated and asset values are understated
options.B: Net profit is overstated indefinitely
options.C: Assets are overstated and liabilities disappear
options.D: No impact on net profit or assets

answer_html: Answer: (A) Net profit for the current year is understated and asset values are understated[cite: 49].

question_html: An expenditure is incurred to increase the productive capacity of an existing machine. According to key classification rules, this is:

options.A: Revenue expenditure because the machine already existed
options.B: Capital expenditure because it enhances earning capacity and productive capacity

answer_html: Answer: (B) Capital expenditure because it enhances earning capacity and productive capacity.

question_html: The relative proportion of the amount involved in a transaction when determining whether to expense or capitalise it relates to which consideration?

options.B: Physical weight of the item

answer_html: Answer: (A) Materiality of the amount involved.
